name: Macroscope
statusNote: Complete and verified. Its pipeline was later consolidated, alongside two sibling engines, into Spectrum; the code is kept.
oneLiner: A Node engine that polls ~13 macro and market RSS feeds, has a local LLM judge each surviving headline's market impact, and posts severity-scored cards to Discord plus a local equity-research-styled dashboard.
stack: Node ≥18, ES modules, no build step

components.name: index.js
components.desc: The main polling loop, with a single-instance lock via a local TCP port

components.name: serve.js
components.desc: Dependency-free static HTTP server for the dashboard

components.name: src/prefilter.js
components.desc: Lexicon bouncer that pre-filters headlines, doubling as the offline fallback

components.name: src/analyze.js
components.desc: The Ollama impact read: market, direction, magnitude, confidence; severity = magnitude × confidence, bucketed 1–4

components.name: src/store.js
components.desc: Capped JSON dedupe file plus a last-60-cards feed for the dashboard

components.name: src/discord.js
components.desc: Paced card posting to a webhook, outbound only

components.name: web/
components.desc: Static dashboard that polls the feed every 30 seconds

dataFlow: RSS feeds are fetched, parsed, and normalized.
Items are deduped against a capped seen-file.
The lexicon pre-filter drops headlines with no market vocabulary.
Survivors go to the local Ollama model for an impact read, with an offline lexicon fallback if the LLM is down.
Severity is computed as magnitude times confidence and bucketed 1–4.
Each card is recorded to the local feed file, which the dashboard polls.
Cards are posted, paced, to a Discord webhook.
decisions: Forked from an earlier doomfeed pipeline but deliberately kept in Node so it could not be imported back into the Python trading tools.
The lexicon was demoted to pre-filter and offline fallback only — the LLM is the brain.
Severity = magnitude × confidence, so low-confidence calls don't read as loud as well-supported ones.
Sentiment only — no trading APIs, no brokerage feeds, not trading advice.
